promptLatex: The claim '$|x| + |x - 6| \ge 6$ for all real $x$' is to be proved. Which proof strategy is most appropriate?
hintLatex: The absolute value expressions change definition at x = 0 and x = 6.
Split the real line into three regions and evaluate the sum in each.
The middle region gives the constant value 6.
solutionLatex:
Split on the breakpoints $x = 0$ and $x = 6$.

- If $x \le 0$: $|x| + |x - 6| = -x + 6 - x = 6 - 2x \ge 6$, since $x \le 0$.
- If $0 \le x \le 6$: $|x| + |x - 6| = x + 6 - x = 6$.
- If $x \ge 6$: $|x| + |x - 6| = x + x - 6 = 2x - 6 \ge 6$, since $x \ge 6$.

Every case gives at least $6$, with equality exactly on $[0, 6]$, so the claim holds for all real $x$.
